work: stress-test this Hyperswarm heartbeat wire-format design — pick the encoding + frame schema + cadence for R-7 cluster discovery, answer Q1-Q4 with concrete recommendations
artifact:
NEOTH R-7 cluster mode runs peeroxide Hyperswarm for peer discovery. Two daemons configured with the same cluster name find each other via the public HyperDHT, establish Noise-encrypted AsyncRead+AsyncWrite streams. peeroxide does NOT define a payload protocol; NEOTH must.

Goal: each peer broadcasts a heartbeat carrying its load + capabilities so the orchestrator (LeastLoaded routing policy) can pick the most idle headroom for each request.

PeerLoad struct on the receive side (already shipped in cluster/mod.rs):
  peer: PeerId (UUID v7 string)
  tokens_per_sec: f64
  inflight_requests: u32
  capabilities: Vec<String>  // ["claude_cli", "openai_compat", ...]
  last_observed: Instant
  healthy: bool

Design space:

Q1 encoding:
  A) JSON lines (one frame per line, easy to grep + debug)
  B) CBOR (compact binary, ~30% smaller than JSON, schema-evolution-friendly)
  C) bincode (tightest packing, Rust-only — Hyperswarm peers must all run NEOTH binaries today, so cross-language isn't a constraint yet)
  D) protobuf (cross-language but big dep + schema files)

Q2 framing:
  A) length-prefixed (u32 LE length + payload bytes)
  B) newline-delimited (only works with JSON, fragile under binary payloads)
  C) noise-frame native (peeroxide already does Noise framing per message, so we can just call write_all + flush per heartbeat)

Q3 cadence:
  A) fixed 5s interval per peer
  B) adaptive (1s when load > 80%, 30s when idle)
  C) on-change only + 60s keepalive

Q4 version negotiation:
  A) version byte first, peer with older byte downgrades (Telegram-style)
  B) protocol-version handshake on connect, peer with older version disconnects (gRPC-style)
  C) no version (v0.1 ship; bump later)

Reviewer task: pick Q1-Q4. Also flag anything missing — should heartbeats include a sequence number for dropped-frame detection? Should there be a separate fast-track for capability changes vs load updates?
